clue.text: Aim to consume spirit, having succeeded in forming legal document

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed in the developing word
to consume something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: an aim is an intent or purpose
rum is a spirit
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a tot of rum before successfully drafting a legal deed.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: 'to consume' signals the spirit going inside the aim, and 'in' then signals the abbreviation going inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument in law is a formal written deed such as a contract or will.

clue.text: Finally exhausts another developed source of oil

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged
finally means the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: One oil source runs dry, so another is opened up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives S, and 'developed' rearranges S with ANOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea between Britain and Norway holds major offshore oilfields.

clue.text: Letter seen in first half of sign

indicators.note: first half of means only the opening three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A letter is spotted in the first part of a signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a star sign, the bull TAURUS, not a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: One visible on the outskirts of Cambridge, say

annotationWithheld.why: 'One visible on the outskirts of Cambridge, say' (5) for UNITY: UNI is Cambridge, say, but no reading of 'visible on the outskirts' gives TY; the OCR text looks garbled and the scan is blank.

clue.text: Block advert for The Listener?

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a plug is a piece of publicity, an advert

explanation.surface: Someone takes out an advertisement block in The Listener magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC weekly magazine, so the surface reads as booking advert space in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug is a stopper put into the ear to block out sound.

clue.text: Sort of marksman in excessive rising quelled by follower of Lao Tzu

indicators.note: quelled by means held down within, so the Taoist surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Lao Tzu founded Taoism, so his follower is a Taoist

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: An overzealous sharpshooter's uprising is calmed by a Taoist sage.
explanation.walkthrough: The rising piece sits just after the first two letters of the Taoist. The definition is playful: this marksman makes marks rather than hitting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist puts marks on skin, so is playfully a mark-making person rather than a shooter.

clue.text: Turn to have good fortune, avoiding the drop

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the drop is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a windfall is a stroke of unexpected good fortune
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: A gambler hopes a turn of the wheel brings luck without a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to turn, as one winds a handle or a clock key.

clue.text: Place in grave beneath wife's fresh plant

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath means the burial word comes below the letter for wife

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to inter is to bury in a grave
green means fresh or new

explanation.surface: A widower places fresh flowers on his wife's grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is a low evergreen plant whose leaves yield an aromatic oil.

clue.text: Harmful without money?

parts.note: no means having none, without
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: Being penniless can do real damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocent is an old word for harmful, the opposite of innocent.

clue.text: One providing better assistance at the wheel?

definitions.text: One providing better assistance at the wheel?

parts.words: One providing better assistance at the wheel?
parts.note: read 'better' as one who bets: the person helping gamblers at the roulette wheel, not a superior driving instructor

explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs the roulette table in a casino, taking and paying out bets for the players.

clue.text: A pair of cards

parts.note: the first of the pair is the card numbered ten
the second of the pair is the ace

explanation.surface: A card player names two cards drawn together from the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the bridge term and also spells out its two named cards side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist a tenace is a combination of two cards of one suit, such as ace and queen, missing the card between.

clue.text: Share last of monkey nuts

parts.note: a whack is a share or portion, as in paying one's whack

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A zookeeper hands out the remaining peanuts to a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacky or whacky is informal for crazy, a sense that nuts also carries.

clue.text: Material about The Mousetrap, say

parts.note: seems to ask for a script about the Agatha Christie play, but means a fabric named after the bait a mousetrap holds

explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecloth is a loose woven cotton fabric originally used for wrapping cheese.

clue.text: Son staying in seaside resort to complete unfinished work

indicators.note: staying in means being placed inside the resort's name

parts.note: Looe is a seaside resort town in Cornwall
to end something is to complete it

explanation.surface: A son on holiday at the coast hopes to finish off some outstanding jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOE is a small fishing and holiday town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail or task left unfinished and still needing attention.

clue.text: Uniform state that's unlikely when camping in the mountains?

definitions.text: Uniform state that's unlikely when camping in the mountains?

parts.words: Uniform state that's unlikely when camping in the mountains?
parts.note: on sloping mountain ground the tent pegs will not be at one height; the phrase for that also means scores being equal

explanation.definitionFit: Level pegging is a British idiom for being exactly even in a contest, from scoring pegs on a cribbage board.

clue.text: Hum without a note in Saint's chant

indicators.note: without means outside, so the smell word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a hum is a bad smell, a pong
la is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A monk hums a note while singing a saint's chant.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a hum or pong is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval church chant sung in unison.

clue.text: Trader having a laugh around about minute, spring

clue.text: Mark allowed in any case, after loud complaint

indicators.note: after places the phrase for in any case behind the letter for loud

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
to let is to allow
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
ever here means at all, in any case

explanation.surface: Someone with a scar is permitted to complain loudly about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an illness, and scarlet fever is an infectious disease with a red rash.

clue.text: Venetian learning nothing about far-off land

parts.note: lore is learning or knowledge
NZ, New Zealand, is a far-off land seen from Britain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Venetian scholar knows nothing about a distant country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorenzo is a Venetian in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice who elopes with Jessica.

clue.text: Our cast filled with semi-molten brass

indicators.note: filled with means the rearranged word holds another piece inside
cast means thrown or moulded into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
semi means half, so only the first half of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Our metal casting is filled with half-melted brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-molten' supplies just the front half of molten; the rearranged 'Our' is split open around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded brass or bronze used to decorate furniture, so it is a kind of brass.

clue.text: Credit bunker shot he's played

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A golfer is given credit for a fine shot out of a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges CR with BUNKER. The golfing words mislead: the answer is a composer whose music is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Bruckner was an Austrian composer whose symphonies orchestras perform, so he is someone played.

clue.text: It might just drive one's onset of blind rage

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: A driver loses their temper in a fit of blind road rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a battered old car that barely runs, so it might just drive.

clue.text: Burn item of clothing right away

indicators.note: away means the right letter is taken off

parts.note: a blazer is a jacket, an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A jacket gets scorched and is promptly thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze is to burn fiercely with flames.

clue.text: Fancy breaking ducks with a couple of centuries, one's first runs

indicators.note: this says the runs letter comes first in the answer

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the ducks apart by going in among them
with here means mixed in among the ducks, so one century sits between two of them

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing, O, so ducks give three Os here
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century; a couple of them gives one C here
the second of the couple of centuries gives another C

explanation.surface: A batsman's innings breaks a run of ducks with two hundreds, his first runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero and a century a hundred runs. 'with' and 'breaking' put one C after each of the first two Os, giving OCOCO after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo describes a highly ornate eighteenth-century style, so as an adjective it means elaborately fancy.

clue.text: A 7 ac strong enough to cause a general collapse?

indicators.note: a collapse brings things down in disorder, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A wind so strong it could knock over a general.
explanation.walkthrough: '7 ac' refers to the answer at 7 across, a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort scale force seven is a near gale, a wind strong but short of a full gale.

clue.text: Urge on European, say, to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A European is urged to get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee, as in gee up, is a call urging a horse or person to go faster.

clue.text: Rural African transport parked by hospital

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A bus waits outside a hospital in an African village.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is the wild rural back country of Africa or Australia, so it describes rural Africa.

clue.text: Third-party fruit?

definitions.meaning: an unwanted third person tagging along with a couple
a sharp green berry grown on a thorny shrub

explanation.definitionFit: To play gooseberry is British slang for being the unwanted extra with a pair of lovers, and it is also a fruit.
